frozenWindow.extensionReason: 7-day window retained because 4685 >= 500 closed reconcilable Pump episodes

population.definition: inside frozen window AND Pump-relevant AND fully self-contained/reconciled

sizeModeMethod.method: Gaussian KDE over log(firstBuySol), Silverman bandwidth; retain modes with density >=5% of the dominant mode; boundaries are intervening density valleys. Outcomes are not used.

answers.oneStrategyWithVariableSizing: YES. The evidence best supports one recurring acquisition-and-management system with configured size tiers and outcome-responsive exit branches.
answers.multipleDistinctPolicies: NOT ESTABLISHED. Distinct exit templates exist, but all recur throughout the seven days and are nested by realized trade path; no separate causal entry policies were tested here.
answers.sizeBandsAsConvictionTiers: LIKELY. Larger pre-outcome entries have progressively more staged exits and stronger economics, but size is only a moderate predictor of the eventual exit branch.
answers.exitDiffersBySize: YES, MODERATELY. Cramer's V and the cross-tab show a real relationship, especially the shift from rapid full exits at the smallest tier to ladders at larger tiers.
answers.dominantArchetype: The coherent parent policy is one initial Pump bonding-curve acquisition followed by rapid full invalidation or staged ladder management. The three-to-five-stage branch contributes most net profit, but it is future-defined and must not be used to select the next entry-study population.

verdict.nextCausalFingerprintPopulation: Use all 4,685 clean, reconciled 2CQ entry episodes as one causal population. Preserve the outcome-blind entry-size mode as a teacher action/conviction label and stratification variable. Do not condition inclusion on the eventual exit archetype.
rationale: All five natural size modes and all major exit branches persist across the frozen chronology.
Size-conditioned modal exit prediction improves only modestly over the global majority, so size does not uniquely identify separate exit policies.
Rapid exits and progressively longer ladders form a nested response to post-entry trade development.
Selecting the profitable ladder branches for entry research would use future information and create leakage.
